---
name: cate-cli
description: Drive Cate browser, terminal, editor, and panel surfaces from a Cate terminal. Browser page automation uses native agent-browser command syntax.
user-invocable: true
---

# Cate CLI

`cate` is available inside Cate terminals and agent shells. It talks to the
current workspace and requires the relevant Settings → CLI permission.

Start by listing panels:

```bash
cate panel list
```

When working repeatedly with one panel, select it for the current agent or
terminal session:

```bash
cate panel set 1a2b3c4d
cate panel current
```

The selection is isolated by a per-terminal CLI session, so other agents and
terminals keep their own targets. Short ids from `panel list`
are accepted. Use `--panel <id>` only as a one-command override. Clear the
selection to return to Cate's automatic focused/grouped resolution:

```bash
cate panel clear
```

Selections can point to any native panel. Browser and terminal commands reject
a selected panel of the wrong type instead of silently controlling another
panel. If a selected panel was closed, select another panel before continuing.

## Browser workflow

Inspect, act, wait, then inspect again:

```bash
cate panel set 1a2b3c4d
cate browser open https://example.com
cate browser snapshot -i
cate browser fill @s1e2 user@example.com
cate browser click @s1e3
cate browser wait --url '**/dashboard'
cate browser snapshot -i
```

Page commands after `cate browser` use agent-browser's native argv directly:

```bash
cate browser snapshot -i --compact
cate browser get text @s1e4
cate browser find role button click
cate browser fill '#email' user@example.com
cate browser press Enter
cate browser scroll down 600
cate browser screenshot --full
cate browser console
cate browser errors
```

Do not use agent-browser's `open` semantics by assumption: Cate defines
`browser open` as opening a new tab. Use `navigate` only when replacing the
active tab is intentional:

```bash
cate browser open https://second.example
cate browser navigate https://replacement.example
cate browser new-panel https://separate.example
```

Cate owns browser identity and presentation. Native session/CDP switching,
native tab management, upload/download paths, batch, setup, servers, and browser
startup flags are unavailable. Use Cate's lifecycle commands:

```bash
cate browser tabs
cate browser new-tab [url]
cate browser select-tab <id>
cate browser close-tab <id>
cate browser viewport desktop
cate browser viewport mobile
cate browser viewport 1024 768
cate browser viewport compact
cate browser resize 640 480
```

The default compact viewport renders at 75% scale. Responsive viewport size and
canvas panel size are independent. `resize` applies only to canvas panels and
has a 400×300 minimum.

Snapshots come from agent-browser's accessibility tree. Cate wraps engine refs
with an observation revision, for example `@s1e4`. A new snapshot invalidates
older refs; take a fresh snapshot instead of retrying `stale-ref`.

Agent actions display a persistent cursor/highlight in the browser panel. User
input immediately takes control back. Screenshots are saved to a Cate-managed
temporary path and the CLI prints that path.

## Other surfaces

```bash
cate editor open src/app.tsx:42
cate panel create terminal
cate panel create canvas
cate panel set <id>
cate panel current
cate panel clear
cate panel close <id>
```

Read a terminal before sending input. `type` does not append Enter:

```bash
cate panel set 1a2b3c4d
cate terminal read
cate terminal type npm test
cate terminal press enter
```

Terminal input goes to whatever currently owns that PTY, including foreground
TUIs. Never send keys until the panel id and current screen are verified.

name: planner
description: Read-only planning specialist that turns gathered evidence into an implementation plan
tools: read, grep, find, ls
---

You are a read-only planning specialist. Turn the parent agent's requirements,
constraints, and gathered evidence into a concrete implementation plan.

Do not modify files. Verify important claims against the workspace when needed,
but keep additional exploration focused. Return a concise plan with:

1. A one-paragraph summary of the approach and why it fits.
2. Ordered, actionable implementation steps with exact files or symbols.
3. Relevant tests or verification for each risky change.
4. Important risks, assumptions, or unresolved questions.

Your plan is advisory. The parent agent will review it, correct it, and submit
the final plan to the user.

---
name: scout
description: Read-only codebase exploration for concise evidence-backed handoffs
tools: read, grep, find, ls
---

You are a read-only codebase scout. Investigate the assigned area quickly and
return concise, evidence-backed findings for the parent agent.

Do not modify files or attempt implementation. Follow imports and call sites as
needed, inspect relevant tests and configuration, and cite exact file paths and
symbols. End with the most important findings, risks, and open questions.

---
name: worker
description: Isolated implementation specialist for a clearly scoped coding task
tools: read, write, edit, bash, grep, find, ls
---

You are an implementation specialist working in an isolated context. Complete
the assigned coding task autonomously and keep changes tightly scoped.

Inspect the relevant code before editing, preserve unrelated work, and verify
your changes with the most relevant tests or checks. Do not delegate to another
subagent.

Return a concise handoff covering what changed, exact files or symbols touched,
verification performed, and any remaining risks or blockers.

Now I have a comprehensive understanding. Let me compile the findings. --- ## Pathfinder System Research Summary ### **Core Architecture** (`game/systems/Pathfinder.ts`) **JPS (Jump Point Search)** - Octile-distance heuristic (8-directional grid) - Pruned successors: natural + forced neighbors - Recursive `jump()` traverses until jump point (turning point / forced neighbor / goal) - Version-stamped node arrays (`nodeG`, `nodeParent`, `nodeOpen`, `nodeVersion`) recycled to avoid GC - Auto-finds nearest unblocked start/end if blocked (expanding rings, max radius 15) **Flow Fields (mass movement)** - Single BFS/Dijkstra from target outward → computes `integration` cost + `dirX/dirY` vectors per cell - Cached by `(targetGridX,targetGridY)` key; invalidated on grid changes (`gridVersion` bump) - LRU cap at 10 entries - `getFlowDirection()` returns normalized vector; returns `null` if field stale (`version` mismatch) or on blocked cell **Async Request Queue** - `requestPath(start, end, callback)` → queued with unique ID - `processQueue()` runs up to `maxPathsPerFrame=20` per frame - `processQueueBudgeted(budget)` for large unit counts (UnitSystem uses 100 when >1000 units) - Queue depth capped at 500; oldest dropped beyond cap **Terrain Cost Layer** - `updateTerrainCosts(terrainSystem, season)` recomputes per-cell cost from biome + season multiplier + river penalty - `BIOME_PATH_COSTS`: deep=999 (impassable), grass=1.0, forest=1.4, swamp=1.5, stone=1.6, etc. - `SEASON_CONFIG[season].movementCostMult`: Winter=1.3, others=1.0 - `applyWaterMask()` marks water cells permanently blocked (never cleared by `markGrid(false)`) **Blocking API** - `markGrid(x,y,w,h,blocked)` for buildings — clears flow cache on any change - `isBlocked(x,y)` checks both building + water masks **Profiling** - `frameStats` (per-frame) + `totals` (cumulative) - `getPerfReport()` returns averages per frame - MainScene calls `beginFrame()` at update start; logs path timing in debug --- ### **Integration Points** | Component | Usage | |---|---| | **MainScene** | Owns `pathfinder` instance; calls `beginFrame()`, `updateTerrainCosts()`, `applyWaterMask()`, `markGrid()` for buildings | | **UnitSystem** | • `commandMove()`: ≥12 units → `generateFlowField()`; <12 → individual `findPath()`
• `commandMoveToQueue()`: per-unit `findPath()` (batched)
• `commandFollowPath()`: segments via `findPath()`
• Chase logic: `requestPath()` async for return-to-anchor & repath
• `moveAlongFlowField()`: `getFlowDirection()` every 80ms per unit
• `moveAlongPath()`: follows JPS waypoints; stale-path policy via `combatPath.ts` | | **BuildingManager** | `markGrid()` on place/demolish | | **EntityFactory** | `markGrid()` on spawn/destroy | | **VillagerSystem** | `findPath()` for resource gathering trips | | **SaveSystem** | Restores building blocks on load | --- ### **Key Constants** ```typescript CELL = 32 // grid resolution (matches tree collision grid) FLOW_FIELD_THRESHOLD = 12 // units to trigger flow field FLOW_STEER_INTERVAL = 80 // ms per unit maxPathsPerFrame = 20 // sync path budget processQueueBudgeted(100) // async budget when >1000 units STALE_PATH_LIFETIME = 5000 // ms CHASE_REPATH_MIN_MS = 450 // anti-thrash ``` --- ### **Path Stability Mechanics** (`game/utils/combatPath.ts`) - `shouldRepathChase()`: avoids thrash — only repaths if target moved >28px, 450ms elapsed, or 2.5s periodic - `findResumePathStep()`: resumes at closest waypoint ahead (never resets to 0 → no walk-back) - `stalePathAction()`: mid-chase → `clear_repath` (stays CHASING); idle → `clear_idle` (drops to IDLE) - `pathEndNearTarget()`: slack 10px — keeps path if end near target --- ### **Performance Notes** - Grid: 2048/32 = 64×64 = 4096 cells (default map) - Float64/Int32/Uint8/Uint16 arrays pre-allocated (no GC during pathfinding) - Flow field BFS uses single `queue[]` array with index pointer - UnitSystem splits work: flow field steering (O(1)/unit) + path queue (batched) + per-frame bucket rotation - Physics bodies disabled for stationary stress-test units (massive savings) --- ### **Open Questions / Risks** 1. **Flow field cache LRU** uses `Map.keys().next().value` — iteration order not guaranteed LRU in all JS engines 2. **Grid version** only bumped implicitly via `flowFieldCache.clear()` in `markGrid`/`updateTerrainCosts`/`applyWaterMask`; `gridVersion` field exists but never incremented — may be vestigial 3. **Water mask** applied at cell centers only; narrow rivers <32px may be missed 4. **Async chase repath** uses `requestPath` callback — unit may die/change state before callback fires (guarded by `if (!unit.scene) return`) 5. **No path smoothing** — JPS returns cell centers; units move point-to-point (visible zigzag on long diagonals)

---

# CivStrategy: System Development Plans

## Summary

Five major system improvements targeting annihilation-scale performance (5000+ units), visual fidelity, and developer experience. Plans are ordered by dependency: Pathfinder first (foundation), then UnitSystem (consumes paths), LiquidCombat (piggybacks on UnitSystem), Atmospheric (independent GPU optimization), React-Phaser bridge (developer-facing). Each phase is independently shippable with measurable perf wins.

---

## 1. Pathfinder Optimization

**Current state:** JPS + flow fields + async queue. ~20 paths/frame budget. Flow field cache (max 10). Per-cell cost map (biome + season). Queue depth cap 500 with drop counter.

**Problems identified:**
- Recursive `jump()` in JPS causes stack overflow risk on large open maps (no iteration limit)
- `processQueueBudgeted` always drains from front — no priority (combat paths starve)
- Flow field cache uses FIFO eviction, not LRU — frequent targets evicted
- `findNearestUnblockedGrid` does expanding ring (brute force) — O(r²) per blocked-end query
- No path smoothing — raw JPS waypoints cause jittery movement

### Phase 1: Safety & Correctness (1-2 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 1a | `game/systems/Pathfinder.ts` | Convert recursive `jump()` to iterative loop. Replace `this.jump(...)` calls with while-loop. Eliminates stack overflow on 100x100+ open grids. |
| 1b | `game/systems/Pathfinder.ts` | Add `JUMP_MAX_STEPS = 512` limit to iterative jump. Return null on limit. Prevents infinite loops on edge cases. |
| 1c | `game/systems/Pathfinder.test.ts` (new) | Unit test: JPS on 100x100 grid, blocked start/end, diagonal-only paths. Use `vi.mock('phaser')` pattern from `ProceduralSoundSystem.test.ts`. |

**Test:** `npm run test` passes. JPS returns valid paths on all blocked/unblocked combos.

### Phase 2: Priority Queue & LRU (2-3 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 2a | `game/systems/Pathfinder.ts` | Replace `requestQueue: PathRequest[]` with priority queue (combat=1, move=2, idle=3). Binary heap, O(log n) insert/pop. |
| 2b | `game/systems/Pathfinder.ts` | Replace `flowFieldCache: Map` with LRU cache class (max 16 entries). Track access time. Evict least-recently-used. |
| 2c | `game/systems/Pathfinder.ts` | Add `PathPriority` enum: `ATTACK=1, MOVE=2, IDLE=3`. Expose in `requestPath()` signature. |

**Test:** Mock 500 queued requests with mixed priorities. Verify attack paths complete first.

### Phase 3: Path Smoothing (2-3 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 3a | `game/systems/Pathfinder.ts` | Add `smoothPath(points): Vector2[]`. Line-of-sight check between waypoints. Remove collinear intermediates. |
| 3b | `game/systems/Pathfinder.ts` | Apply smoothing in `findPath()` return. Gate behind `SMOOTH_PATHS = true` constant. |
| 3c | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Remove redundant point-skipping in `moveAlongPath()` (currently skips points < 4px — smoothing handles this). |

**Test:** Visually verify smoother movement in stress test (1000 units, mixed terrain).

### Phase 4: Blocked-Cell Nearest Search (1 day)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 4a | `game/systems/Pathfinder.ts` | Replace `findNearestUnblockedGrid()` expanding ring with BFS from target. Cache result per-frame (reset in `beginFrame()`). |

**Perf target:** `findPath()` with blocked end: < 0.1ms (was ~0.5ms on 2048x2048 maps).

---

## 2. UnitSystem Enhancements

**Current state:** 1764 lines. Bucket-based update (300/frame). SpatialHash for neighbors. Scan throttle 500ms. Flow field threshold 12 units. Separation interval adaptive (3-60 frames). Charge impulse + front-rank lock.

**Problems identified:**
- `updateUnitLogicTimed` + `applyLiquidSteering` called per unit per bucket — double iteration over same unit
- `applySeparation` does full O(n) sweep every 3-60 frames — at 5000 units this is 5000 SpatialHash queries
- `scanForTargets` builds `_engageCache` per scan call (redundant when multiple idle units scan same frame)
- Path memory cap (200) is hardcoded — too small for large maps, too large for small maps
- No distance-LOD for combat logic — units 2000px away still run full state machine

### Phase 1: Iteration Fusion (1-2 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 1a | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Merge `updateUnitLogicTimed` + `applyLiquidSteering` into single `updateUnitFull(unit, time)` call in bucket loop. Eliminates double function call overhead. |
| 1b | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Pre-compute `unit.flowTarget` and `unit.flowField` in a single pass before bucket loop (already done — just verify). |

**Test:** Unit count unchanged. Profile bucket loop: should show ~15% fewer calls.

### Phase 2: Separation Optimization (2-3 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 2a | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Replace full-sweep `applySeparation()` with per-cell iteration. Only iterate occupied SpatialHash cells (not all units). ~30-50% fewer queries at 5000 units. |
| 2b | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Cache separation results per-cell per-frame. Reuse in `applyLiquidSteering()` (velocity alignment already piggybacks). |
| 2c | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Add `SEPARATION_RADIUS_SQ = 324` constant (precomputed). Replace `distSq < 324` check with constant comparison. |

**Test:** 5000-unit stress test. Separation frame time: < 2ms (was ~5ms).

### Phase 3: Target Scan Optimization (2 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 3a | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Move `_buildEngagementMap()` to `update()` top-level (once per frame, not per scan). Store as `_engagementMap`. |
| 3b | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | In `scanForTargets()`, read `_engagementMap` instead of rebuilding. |
| 3c | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Add distance-LOD: units > 500px from nearest enemy use `scanInterval = 1000ms` (was 500ms for all). |

**Test:** Profile scan phase. Target: < 1ms/frame at 3000 combat units.

### Phase 4: Adaptive Path Memory (1 day)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 4a | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Replace hardcoded `200` with `maxPathLength = Math.min(300, Math.max(80, mapWidth / 10))`. Scale with map size. |
| 4b | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Add `unit.pathMemoryUsed` tracker. Log when cap hit (debug mode only). |

**Test:** 4096x4096 map. Verify no path truncation at default zoom.

---

## 3. LiquidCombat Scaling

**Current state:** Pressure grid (SpatialHash cells), contact lines (formation pairs), velocity alignment. All precomputed in `precompute()` before UnitSystem bucket pass. Per-unit forces applied in `applyLiquidSteering()`.

**Problems identified:**
- `precompute()` iterates all units twice (pressure + contact). At 5000 units, ~1ms per pass.
- Contact line detection uses AABB gap between formations — breaks when formations overlap (gap = 0, strength = 1 for all pairs).
- `getContactForce()` linearly scans all contact lines per unit — O(units × contactLines). At 200 contact lines + 3000 units = 600K iterations.
- Velocity alignment queries SpatialHash per unit — duplicate of separation query.
- `isCivilian()` check runs per unit per phase — branch prediction friendly but redundant when called 3x per unit.

### Phase 1: Precompute Fusion (1-2 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 1a | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.ts` | Merge pressure grid + contact line detection into single unit iteration. Build both structures in one pass over `allUnits`. Eliminates O(n) second pass. |
| 1b | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.ts` | Pre-filter civilian check once at top: `const military = allUnits.filter(u => !isCivilian(u))`. Use `military` for both passes. |
| 1c | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.ts` | Cache `military` array per-frame. Reuse in `getAlignmentVelocity()`. |

**Test:** 5000-unit stress test. `precompute()` time: < 0.5ms (was ~1ms).

### Phase 2: Contact Line Optimization (2-3 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 2a | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.ts` | Add contact line spatial index: `Map<string, ContactLine[]>` keyed by grid cell. `getContactForce()` queries only nearby cells instead of scanning all lines. |
| 2b | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.ts` | Fix AABB overlap bug: when `gap < 0`, set `strength = 1.0` (fully engaged) instead of `1 - 0/COUNTACT_RANGE`. |
| 2c | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.ts` | Cap `contactLines` array at 500. Sort by strength descending. Drop weakest beyond cap. |

**Test:** 2000-unit battle (1000v1000). Contact line count: < 200. `getContactForce()` time: < 0.1ms.

### Phase 3: Velocity Alignment Deduplication (1-2 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 3a | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.ts` | Remove `getAlignmentVelocity()` SpatialHash query. Use separation's cached neighbor list. |
| 3b | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Pass separation neighbors to `liquidCombat.applyAlignment(unit, neighbors)`. Avoid second query. |
| 3c | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.ts` | `applyAlignment(unit, neighbors)`: compute avg velocity from pre-fetched neighbors. |

**Test:** Profile `applyLiquidSteering()` per unit. Target: < 0.05ms (was ~0.1ms).

### Phase 4: Force Tuning & Debug Visualization (2 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 4a | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.ts` | Add `debugForceGraphics` (optional). Draw pressure arrows, contact normals. Gate behind `scene.debugMode`. |
| 4b | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.ts` | Tune constants: `PRESSURE_FORCE_MAX`, `CONTACT_BACKWARD_FORCE`, `ALIGN_STRENGTH` based on stress test. |
| 4c | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.test.ts` (new) | Unit tests for pressure gradient calculation, contact line detection, alignment averaging. |

**Test:** Visual: armies collide → front compresses → lateral flow visible. Perf: 5000-unit battle < 2ms total liquid combat.

---

## 4. Atmospheric Performance

**Current state:** 20 cloud sprites, bloom (PostFX), vignette, seasonal tint (Graphics.fillRect), wind sway (sine). PostFX toggle. Seasonal tint dirty flag.

**Problems identified:**
- Bloom is a full-screen GPU pass — dominates frame time on iGPUs (Intel UHD, M1 integrated)
- 20 cloud sprites each updated every frame — O(20) per frame even when zoomed out (clouds invisible)
- Seasonal tint `fillRect` covers entire viewport even when alpha ~ 0 — wasted GPU fill
- `getWindSway()` called per-tree per-frame — no caching, redundant sine computation
- No LOD: atmospheric effects run at same cost regardless of zoom level

### Phase 1: Cloud Culling (1 day)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 1a | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Add viewport culling to cloud update. Skip update for clouds outside camera bounds + 500px padding. |
| 1b | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Pool cloud sprites: max 12 active, recycle off-screen clouds. Reduce from 20 to 12. |
| 1c | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Skip cloud update entirely when `cam.zoom < 0.5` (zoomed out — clouds invisible). |

**Test:** Profile cloud update. Target: < 0.1ms (was ~0.3ms).

### Phase 2: Bloom Adaptive Quality (2 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 2a | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Add zoom-based bloom resolution: `bloomQuality = clamp(cam.zoom, 0.25, 1.0)`. Lower zoom = lower resolution bloom pass. |
| 2b | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Add FPS-gated bloom: if FPS < 30 for 2 consecutive seconds, reduce `bloomEffect.strength` by 20%. Restore when FPS > 45. |
| 2c | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Add `setBloomQuality(quality: 'high' | 'medium' | 'low')` method. Low = no bloom, Medium = half-res, High = full. |

**Test:** Intel UHD 620 benchmark. Bloom cost: < 2ms (was ~5ms).

### Phase 3: Wind Sway Cache (1 day)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 3a | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Cache wind sway per-position: `Map<string, { value: number; time: number }>`. Reuse for 100ms. |
| 3b | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Quantize positions to 32px grid before cache lookup. Reduce cache size. |
| 3c | `game/systems/CullingSystem.ts` | Call `atmosphericSystem.getWindSway()` in tree visual update (already has per-tree iteration). |

**Test:** 1000 visible trees. Wind sway cost: < 0.05ms (was ~0.2ms).

### Phase 4: Seasonal Tint Optimization (1 day)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 4a | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Skip `fillRect` when `alpha < 0.005`. Already partially implemented — verify no edge cases. |
| 4b | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Use `Phaser.GameObjects.Rectangle` instead of `Graphics` for seasonal tint. Avoids Graphics clear/fill overhead. |
| 4c | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Cache tint color/alpha. Only create new Rectangle when target changes (not every frame). |

**Test:** Profile seasonal tint. Target: < 0.05ms (was ~0.3ms on large viewport).

---

## 5. React-Phaser Bridge Improvements

**Current state:** Dual-channel bridge. React→Phaser via `window.dispatchEvent(CustomEvent)` → `App.tsx` bridge → `gameInstance.events.emit()`. Phaser→React via `scene.events.emit(EVENTS.UPDATE_STATS, ...)` → `App.tsx` listener → `setStats()`. 20+ event types in `EVENTS` constant.

**Problems identified:**
- `setStats()` called every frame (60fps) triggers full React re-render tree — `GameUI` + children
- `window.dispatchEvent(CustomEvent)` for React→Phaser is indirect — adds DOM event overhead
- No event batching: rapid selection changes fire multiple `SELECTION_CHANGED` events
- `PhaserGame.tsx` recreates game instance on every prop change (faction, mapMode, etc.) — full destroy/recreate
- No cleanup verification: event listeners added in `useEffect` may leak if `gameInstance` changes

### Phase 1: Stats Throttling (1-2 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 1a | `game/MainScene.ts` | Throttle `UPDATE_STATS` emission: emit max 10fps (100ms interval), not 60fps. |
| 1b | `App.tsx` | Add `useMemo` for `GameUI` props derived from `stats`. Prevent unnecessary re-renders. |
| 1c | `components/GameUI.tsx` | Add `React.memo()` to `GameUI` component. Compare `stats` shallow-equal. |

**Test:** Profile React render. Target: 10 re-renders/sec (was 60). No visual lag on resource counters.

### Phase 2: Direct Bridge (2-3 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 2a | `App.tsx` | Replace `window.dispatchEvent(CustomEvent)` with `gameInstance.events.emit()` directly. Store `gameInstance` in ref (already available). |
| 2b | `App.tsx` | Remove all `window.addEventListener('...')` handlers in `useEffect`. Replace with direct `gameInstance.events.emit()`. |
| 2c | `constants.ts` | Add missing event names to `EVENTS` object (currently using magic strings like `'request-set-formation'`, `'clear-selection'`, `'save-game'`). |

**Test:** Verify all React→Phaser commands work (build, spawn, formation, stance, research, save/load).

### Phase 3: Event Batching (2-3 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 3a | `game/MainScene.ts` | Add `emitBatched(event, data, intervalMs)`: queue event, emit at most once per `intervalMs`. |
| 3b | `game/MainScene.ts` | Apply batching to `SELECTION_CHANGED`, `UPDATE_STATS`, `BUILDING_SELECTED`. |
| 3c | `components/GameUI.tsx` | Use `useDeferredValue` for `selectedCount` to defer non-critical UI updates. |

**Test:** Rapid selection changes (click 10 units in 100ms). Verify single `SELECTION_CHANGED` emission.

### Phase 4: Game Lifecycle Safety (1-2 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 4a | `components/PhaserGame.tsx` | Add `useRef` guard: skip destroy/recreate if only `stressTestConfig` changes. Use `game.scene.restart()` instead. |
| 4b | `App.tsx` | Add cleanup verification: in `useEffect` return, check `gameInstance.events.off()` for all listeners. Log warning if any missing. |
| 4c | `App.tsx` | Add `useEffect` dependency audit: ensure `gameInstance` is the only dependency for bridge listener setup. |

**Test:** Start game → quit → restart. No console errors, no leaked listeners.

---

## Dependency Graph

```
Phase 1 (all systems)  →  Phase 2  →  Phase 3  →  Phase 4
     ↑                      ↑           ↑           ↑
  Pathfinder             UnitSystem  LiquidCombat  Atmospheric
  (foundation)           (consumes)  (piggybacks)  (independent)
```

**Recommended order:** Pathfinder P1 → UnitSystem P1 → LiquidCombat P1 → Atmospheric P1 → (all P2 in parallel) → (all P3 in parallel) → (all P4 in parallel).

---

## Risks & Assumptions

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| JPS iterative conversion may change path output | Unit test: compare old recursive vs new iterative on 100 grids. Paths must be identical. |
| Priority queue introduces latency for idle units | Cap idle priority queue depth at 1000. Drop oldest idle paths beyond cap. |
| Contact line spatial index may double memory | Cap at 500 lines. Monitor `performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize`. |
| Bloom adaptive quality may cause visual pops | Lerp bloom strength over 2 seconds, not instant. |
| React throttle may cause stale stats display | Show "..." indicator when stats are stale > 500ms. |
| Direct bridge bypasses DOM event bus | No dependency — Phaser events are in-process. DOM events were always redundant. |

---

## Unresolved Questions

1. **Pathfinder:** Should JPS support weighted grids (biome costs) or stick to uniform? Current implementation treats costs as post-hoc — may produce suboptimal paths in heterogeneous terrain.
2. **LiquidCombat:** Should contact lines support more than 2 owners (free-for-all)? Current code assumes binary owner=0 vs owner=1.
3. **Atmospheric:** Should bloom be user-configurable per quality preset (Low/Medium/High/Custom)? Currently only a single slider.
4. **React-Phaser:** Should stats emission be pushed from MainScene or pulled by React (polling)? Push is simpler but creates coupling.

# GEMINI.md - CivStrategy RTS Technical Specification

> **Purpose**: This document provides LLMs with essential technical context about the CivStrategy RTS game project to minimize token waste and maximize development efficiency.

---

## Project Overview

**CivStrategy** is a Civilization-style Real-Time Strategy (RTS) game built with **Phaser 3**, **React**, and **TypeScript**. It features:
- Faction-based gameplay (Romans, Gauls, Carthage)
- Resource management (Wood, Food, Gold)
- Building construction and economy systems
- Combat units with formations and stances
- Fog of War, infinite/fixed map modes, AI opponents
- Atmospheric effects (bloom, particles, vignette)

---

## Technology Stack

| Layer | Technology | Version |
|-------|-----------|---------|
| **Game Engine** | Phaser 3 | ^3.80.0 |
| **Frontend** | React | ^18.2.0 |
| **Language** | TypeScript | ^5.2.2 |
| **Build Tool** | Vite | ^5.2.0 |
| **Styling** | Tailwind CSS | ^3.4.3 |
| **Linting** | ESLint 9 | ^9.39.2 |
| **UI Icons** | lucide-react | ^0.562.0 |

---

## Project Structure

```
CivStrategy/
├── game/                          # Phaser game logic (core engine)
│   ├── MainScene.ts              # Main Phaser scene (coordinates all systems)
│   ├── systems/                  # Game systems (ECS-like architecture)
│   │   ├── AtmosphericSystem.ts  # Bloom, particles, atmospheric effects
│   │   ├── BuildingManager.ts    # Building placement, demolition, territory
│   │   ├── CullingSystem.ts      # Performance: off-screen entity culling
│   │   ├── EconomySystem.ts      # Resource gathering, production rates
│   │   ├── EnemyAISystem.ts      # AI faction logic
│   │   ├── EntityFactory.ts      # Spawning combat units & buildings
│   │   ├── FeedbackSystem.ts     # Visual feedback (selection circles, etc.)
│   │   ├── FogOfWarSystem.ts     # Vision & fog rendering
│   │   ├── FormationSystem.ts    # Unit formation calculations
│   │   ├── InfiniteMapSystem.ts  # Infinite map chunk generation
│   │   ├── InputManager.ts       # Mouse/keyboard input handling
│   │   ├── MapGenerationSystem.ts# Procedural terrain generation
│   │   ├── MinimapSystem.ts      # Minimap rendering & interaction
│   │   ├── Pathfinder.ts         # A* pathfinding
│   │   ├── SquadSystem.ts        # Visual squad rendering (soldiers)
│   │   ├── UnitSystem.ts         # Combat unit movement, combat, AI
│   │   └── VillagerSystem.ts     # Villager management (static resources)
│   └── utils/
│       ├── iso.ts                # Isometric coordinate conversion
│       ├── Noise.ts              # Perlin noise for terrain
│       └── SpatialHash.ts        # Spatial partitioning for performance
├── components/                   # React UI components
│   ├── GameUI.tsx                # Main in-game HUD
│   ├── LoadingScreen.tsx         # Loading screen
│   ├── MainMenu.tsx              # Main menu & game settings
│   └── PhaserGame.tsx            # React wrapper for Phaser game
├── App.tsx                       # React app entry point
├── index.tsx                     # DOM mount point
├── types.ts                      # TypeScript type definitions
├── constants.ts                  # Game constants (stats, costs, etc.)
├── *.png                         # Asset files (sprites, textures)
├── package.json                  # Dependencies & scripts
├── tsconfig.json                 # TypeScript configuration
├── vite.config.ts                # Vite bundler config
└── eslint.config.js              # ESLint rules
```

---

## Core Architecture

### 1. System-Based Design (ECS-like)

The game follows a **system-based architecture** where each system manages a specific domain:

- **MainScene.ts**: Orchestrates all systems, holds global state (resources, population, happiness)
- **Systems** (`game/systems/`): Independent modules that handle specific responsibilities
- **Communication**: Systems communicate via Phaser events (see `EVENTS` in `constants.ts`)

### 2. Data Flow

```
User Input (React UI) 
    → Phaser Events (EVENTS)
    → MainScene (state container)
    → Systems (game logic)
    → Phaser Scene (rendering)
    → React UI (stats update via events)
```

**Example**: Building a house
1. User clicks "Build House" in `GameUI.tsx`
2. `App.tsx` emits `EVENTS.BUILD_MODE_TOGGLED` event
3. `BuildingManager` listens and enters build mode
4. On click, `BuildingManager.tryBuild()` validates placement
5. `EntityFactory.spawnBuilding()` creates the building
6. `EconomySystem` updates resource rates
7. `MainScene.syncVisuals()` emits `EVENTS.UPDATE_STATS`
8. `GameUI.tsx` re-renders with new stats

### 3. Coordinate System

The game uses **isometric coordinates**:
- **World Coordinates**: Cartesian (x, y) for game logic
- **Screen Coordinates**: Isometric projection for rendering
- **Conversion**: `toIso(x, y)` and `toCartesian(isoX, isoY)` in `game/utils/iso.ts`

---

## Key Files & Their Responsibilities

### 📁 Core Game Files

| File | Purpose | Key Exports/Features |
|------|---------|---------------------|
| **types.ts** | Type definitions | `FactionType`, `UnitType`, `BuildingType`, `GameStats`, `UnitState`, `FormationType`, `UnitStance`, `GameUnit`, `VillagerData` interfaces |
| **constants.ts** | Game configuration | `BUILDINGS`, `UNIT_STATS`, `FACTION_COLORS`, `EVENTS`, `TILE_SIZE`, `FORMATION_BONUSES` |
| **MainScene.ts** | Game coordinator | Initializes all systems, manages resources/population/happiness, handles game speed, emits UI updates |

### 📁 Critical Systems

| System | Responsibility | Key Methods |
|--------|---------------|-------------|
| **UnitSystem** | Combat unit movement, combat, formations, stances | `commandMove()`, `commandAttack()`, `setFormation()`, `setStance()`, `updateUnitLogic()` |
| **VillagerSystem** | Villager management (static resources) | `spawnVillager()`, `assignJob()`, `getIdleVillagers()`, `sendToRallyPoint()` |
| **BuildingManager** | Building placement, demolition, territory | `enterBuildMode()`, `tryBuild()`, `demolishBuilding()`, `drawTerritory()` |
| **EconomySystem** | Resource gathering, worker assignment | `tickEconomy()`, `tickPopulation()`, `assignJobs()` (queries VillagerSystem) |
| **EntityFactory** | Spawning combat units & buildings | `spawnBuilding()`, `spawnUnit()` (combat units only) |
| **InputManager** | User input | Handles drag selection, right-click movement, attack commands, waypoints |
| **SquadSystem** | Visual squads | Renders individual soldiers for units (e.g., 16 soldiers for Pikesman) |
| **FogOfWarSystem** | Vision & fog | Manages explored/visible areas, reveals fog based on unit vision |
| **MinimapSystem** | Minimap | Renders minimap, handles minimap clicks for camera navigation |

### 📁 React Components

| Component | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| **App.tsx** | Main React component, bridges Phaser ↔ React, manages game lifecycle |
| **GameUI.tsx** | In-game HUD (resources, building menu, unit training, formations, stances) |
| **MainMenu.tsx** | Faction selection, map mode/size, fog of war, peaceful mode, AI toggle |
| **PhaserGame.tsx** | Phaser game container (mounts Phaser into React) |

---

## Game Mechanics

### Resources
- **Wood**: From Lumber Camps (requires worker)
- **Food**: From Farms (requires worker) or Hunter's Lodges (requires worker, gathers animals)
- **Gold**: From tax rate (% of population)

### Units

| Unit Type | HP | Attack | Range | Speed | Squad Size | Role | Type |
|-----------|----|----|-------|-------|------------|------|------|
| **Villager** | N/A | N/A | N/A | 80 | 1 | Resource gathering | Static Resource |
| **Pikesman** | 200 | 15 | 40 | 100 | 16 | Standard infantry | Combat Unit |
| **Cavalry** | 400 | 20 | 40 | 160 | 6 | Fast, heavy cavalry | Combat Unit |
| **Legion** | 2000 | 10 | 40 | 70 | 100 | Massive infantry | Combat Unit |
| **Archer** | 150 | 12 | 200 | 90 | 10 | Ranged unit | Combat Unit |
| **Animal** | N/A | N/A | N/A | 40 | 1 | Resource (food) | Static Resource |

### Formations

| Formation | Attack Bonus | Defense Bonus | Speed Multiplier |
|-----------|--------------|---------------|------------------|
| **Box** | +0% | +0% | 1.0x |
| **Line** | +20% | +0% | 0.8x |
| **Circle** | +0% | +25% | 0.7x |
| **Skirmish** | +0% | +15% | 1.1x |
| **Wedge** | +10% | +0% | 1.2x |

### Unit Stances

| Stance | Behavior |
|--------|----------|
| **Aggressive** | Chase enemies indefinitely |
| **Defensive** | Chase briefly, return to anchor point |
| **Hold** | Stand ground, only attack in range |

### Buildings

- **Town Center**: Main hub, provides territory & population
- **House**: +8 max population
- **Farm**: Requires worker, generates food
- **Lumber Camp**: Requires worker, generates wood
- **Hunter's Lodge**: Requires worker, gathers nearby animals for food
- **Barracks**: Trains combat units (Pikesman, Archer, Cavalry)
- **Bonfire**: Provides territory & happiness
- **Small Park**: +5 happiness

---

## Events System

**Location**: `constants.ts → EVENTS`

All Phaser ↔ React communication happens via custom events:

```typescript
export const EVENTS = {
  UPDATE_STATS: 'update-stats',           // MainScene → GameUI (stats update)
  SELECTION_CHANGED: 'selection-changed', // InputManager → GameUI (units selected)
  BUILDING_SELECTED: 'building-selected', // BuildingManager → GameUI (building selected)
  BUILD_MODE_TOGGLED: 'build-mode-toggled', // GameUI → BuildingManager
  TOGGLE_DEMOLISH: 'toggle-demolish',     // GameUI → BuildingManager
  SET_TAX_RATE: 'set-tax-rate',           // GameUI → MainScene
  REGROW_FOREST: 'regrow-forest',         // GameUI → BuildingManager
  CENTER_CAMERA: 'center-camera',         // GameUI → MainScene
  SET_GAME_SPEED: 'set-game-speed',       // GameUI → MainScene
  MINIMAP_CLICK: 'minimap-click',         // MinimapSystem → MainScene
  DEMOLISH_SELECTED: 'demolish-selected', // GameUI → BuildingManager
  SET_BLOOM_INTENSITY: 'set-bloom-intensity' // GameUI → AtmosphericSystem
};
```

**Usage Example**:
```typescript
// React → Phaser
scene.events.emit(EVENTS.SET_TAX_RATE, newTaxRate);

// Phaser → React
scene.events.emit(EVENTS.UPDATE_STATS, gameStats);
```

---

## Important Patterns & Conventions

### 1. Unit State Machine

Units (`UnitSystem.ts`) follow a state machine:

```typescript
export enum UnitState {
  IDLE = 'idle',
  MOVING_TO_WORK = 'moving_to_work',
  WORKING = 'working',
  MOVING_TO_RALLY = 'moving_to_rally',
  WANDERING = 'wandering',
  CHASING = 'chasing',
  ATTACKING = 'attacking'
}
```

State transitions happen in `UnitSystem.updateUnitLogic()`.

### 2. Entity Data Storage

Phaser GameObjects store custom data via:
- **Method 1**: `obj.setData('key', value)` / `obj.getData('key')`
- **Method 2**: Direct properties (e.g., `unit.unitType`, `unit.state`)

**GameUnit Interface** (`types.ts`): Extends `Phaser.GameObjects.Image` with typed properties.

### 3. Squad System

Combat units are visually represented as squads:
- **Main Unit**: Invisible Phaser.Image (holds logic, HP, position)
- **Visual Container**: `unit.visual` (Phaser.Container with soldier sprites)
- **SquadSystem**: Updates visual soldier positions in formations

### 4. Pathfinding

- **Pathfinder.ts**: A* implementation
- **Obstacles**: Trees, buildings
- **Dynamic Paths**: Units recalculate paths if blocked

---

## Build & Development

### NPM Scripts

```bash
npm run dev        # Start Vite dev server
npm run build      # Build for production
npm run lint       # Run ESLint
npm run lint:fix   # Auto-fix ESLint errors
```

**Important**: The user has requested **NOT** to run `npm run build` or `npm run dev` automatically unless explicitly asked.

### Key Files for Configuration

- **tsconfig.json**: TypeScript compiler options (strict mode enabled)
- **eslint.config.js**: ESLint rules (`@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` enforced)
- **vite.config.ts**: Vite bundler configuration
- **package.json**: Dependencies, scripts, Husky pre-commit hooks

---

## Common Tasks for LLMs

### Adding a New Building Type

1. Add enum to `BuildingType` in `types.ts`
2. Add definition to `BUILDINGS` in `constants.ts`
3. Add UI button in `GameUI.tsx` (use `getBuildingsByCategory()`)
4. Handle special logic in `BuildingManager.ts` if needed

### Adding a New Unit Type

1. Add enum to `UnitType` in `types.ts`
2. Add stats to `UNIT_STATS` and `UNIT_VISION` in `constants.ts`
3. Update `EntityFactory.spawnUnit()` to handle spawning
4. Add training UI in `GameUI.tsx` (barracks section)
5. Handle unit-specific logic in `UnitSystem.ts`

### Modifying Unit Behavior

- **Movement**: `UnitSystem.commandMove()`, `UnitSystem.updateUnitLogic()`
- **Combat**: `UnitSystem.commandAttack()`, `UnitSystem.performAttack()`
- **AI**: `UnitSystem.scanForTargets()`, `UnitSystem.handleCombatState()`

### Adding New Events

1. Add event name to `EVENTS` in `constants.ts`
2. Emit event: `scene.events.emit(EVENTS.YOUR_EVENT, data)`
3. Listen in relevant system/component: `scene.events.on(EVENTS.YOUR_EVENT, handler)`

### Fixing Lint Errors

- **No Explicit Any**: Replace `any` with proper types (use `GameUnit`, `BuildingDef`, etc.)
- **Unused Variables**: Remove or prefix with `_` (e.g., `_delta`)
- **Type Assertions**: Use `as Type` sparingly, prefer type guards

---

## Performance Considerations

1. **CullingSystem**: Disables off-screen entities to save CPU
2. **SpatialHash**: Spatial partitioning for fast collision queries
3. **Squad Visuals**: Soldiers are lightweight sprites, not full units
4. **Pathfinding**: Cached, time-limited (paths expire after 5s)
5. **Fog of War**: Rendered to RenderTexture for efficiency

---

## Debugging Tips

- **Enable Debug Visuals**: 
  - `UnitSystem.drawUnitPaths()`: Shows unit paths
  - `BuildingManager.updateHighlights()`: Shows building placement validity
- **Console Logs**: Most systems have commented `console.log()` for debugging
- **Phaser Inspector**: Use browser devtools + Phaser debug draw

---

## Known Quirks & Gotchas

1. **Isometric Rendering**: Always convert world → iso coords before rendering
2. **Unit Selection**: Combat units use `setData('selected', true)` for selection state
3. **Squad HP**: HP is stored on main unit object, not individual soldiers
4. **Barracks Waypoints**: Each barracks has its own waypoint (stored in `customWaypoint` data)
5. **Static Resources**: Villagers and Animals are lightweight static resources (not physics objects, non-selectable, non-targetable)
6. **Villager Management**: Villagers are managed by `VillagerSystem`, not `UnitSystem`
7. **Formation Bonuses**: Applied in `UnitSystem.performAttack()` calculations for combat units only

---

## Future Considerations

- **Technologies**: Currently uses Phaser 3, React, TypeScript, Vite
- **Modularity**: Systems are loosely coupled via events
- **Extensibility**: Easy to add new unit types, buildings, formations
- **Testing**: Currently no test framework (consider Vitest for future)

---

## Quick Reference: File Sizes

| Category | File Count | Notes |
|----------|-----------|-------|
| **Systems** | 17 | All in `game/systems/` (includes VillagerSystem) |
| **Utilities** | 3 | `iso.ts`, `Noise.ts`, `SpatialHash.ts` |
| **React Components** | 4 | `GameUI.tsx` is largest (~36KB) |
| **Total LoC** | ~3700+ | Excluding node_modules |

---

## Conclusion

This document provides a **high-level technical map** of the CivStrategy RTS codebase. When working on this project:

1. **Check `types.ts` and `constants.ts` first** for data structures and configuration
2. **Follow the event-driven architecture** for Phaser ↔ React communication
3. **Use the system-based design** to isolate changes to specific domains
4. **Respect the isometric coordinate system** for rendering
5. **Refer to existing systems** for patterns (e.g., `UnitSystem` for complex logic)

By following these guidelines, LLMs can efficiently navigate and modify the codebase without unnecessary token expenditure.

---

# CivStrategy: System Development Plans

## Summary

Five major system improvements targeting annihilation-scale performance (5000+ units), visual fidelity, and developer experience. Plans are ordered by dependency: Pathfinder first (foundation), then UnitSystem (consumes paths), LiquidCombat (piggybacks on UnitSystem), Atmospheric (independent GPU optimization), React-Phaser bridge (developer-facing). Each phase is independently shippable with measurable perf wins.

---

## 1. Pathfinder Optimization

**Current state:** JPS + flow fields + async queue. ~20 paths/frame budget. Flow field cache (max 10). Per-cell cost map (biome + season). Queue depth cap 500 with drop counter.

**Problems identified:**
- Recursive `jump()` in JPS causes stack overflow risk on large open maps (no iteration limit)
- `processQueueBudgeted` always drains from front — no priority (combat paths starve)
- Flow field cache uses FIFO eviction, not LRU — frequent targets evicted
- `findNearestUnblockedGrid` does expanding ring (brute force) — O(r²) per blocked-end query
- No path smoothing — raw JPS waypoints cause jittery movement

### Phase 1: Safety & Correctness (1-2 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 1a | `game/systems/Pathfinder.ts` | Convert recursive `jump()` to iterative loop. Replace `this.jump(...)` calls with while-loop. Eliminates stack overflow on 100x100+ open grids. |
| 1b | `game/systems/Pathfinder.ts` | Add `JUMP_MAX_STEPS = 512` limit to iterative jump. Return null on limit. Prevents infinite loops on edge cases. |
| 1c | `game/systems/Pathfinder.test.ts` (new) | Unit test: JPS on 100x100 grid, blocked start/end, diagonal-only paths. Use `vi.mock('phaser')` pattern from `ProceduralSoundSystem.test.ts`. |

**Test:** `npm run test` passes. JPS returns valid paths on all blocked/unblocked combos.

### Phase 2: Priority Queue & LRU (2-3 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 2a | `game/systems/Pathfinder.ts` | Replace `requestQueue: PathRequest[]` with priority queue (combat=1, move=2, idle=3). Binary heap, O(log n) insert/pop. |
| 2b | `game/systems/Pathfinder.ts` | Replace `flowFieldCache: Map` with LRU cache class (max 16 entries). Track access time. Evict least-recently-used. |
| 2c | `game/systems/Pathfinder.ts` | Add `PathPriority` enum: `ATTACK=1, MOVE=2, IDLE=3`. Expose in `requestPath()` signature. |

**Test:** Mock 500 queued requests with mixed priorities. Verify attack paths complete first.

### Phase 3: Path Smoothing (2-3 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 3a | `game/systems/Pathfinder.ts` | Add `smoothPath(points): Vector2[]`. Line-of-sight check between waypoints. Remove collinear intermediates. |
| 3b | `game/systems/Pathfinder.ts` | Apply smoothing in `findPath()` return. Gate behind `SMOOTH_PATHS = true` constant. |
| 3c | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Remove redundant point-skipping in `moveAlongPath()` (currently skips points < 4px — smoothing handles this). |

**Test:** Visually verify smoother movement in stress test (1000 units, mixed terrain).

### Phase 4: Blocked-Cell Nearest Search (1 day)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 4a | `game/systems/Pathfinder.ts` | Replace `findNearestUnblockedGrid()` expanding ring with BFS from target. Cache result per-frame (reset in `beginFrame()`). |

**Perf target:** `findPath()` with blocked end: < 0.1ms (was ~0.5ms on 2048x2048 maps).

---

## 2. UnitSystem Enhancements

**Current state:** 1764 lines. Bucket-based update (300/frame). SpatialHash for neighbors. Scan throttle 500ms. Flow field threshold 12 units. Separation interval adaptive (3-60 frames). Charge impulse + front-rank lock.

**Problems identified:**
- `updateUnitLogicTimed` + `applyLiquidSteering` called per unit per bucket — double iteration over same unit
- `applySeparation` does full O(n) sweep every 3-60 frames — at 5000 units this is 5000 SpatialHash queries
- `scanForTargets` builds `_engageCache` per scan call (redundant when multiple idle units scan same frame)
- Path memory cap (200) is hardcoded — too small for large maps, too large for small maps
- No distance-LOD for combat logic — units 2000px away still run full state machine

### Phase 1: Iteration Fusion (1-2 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 1a | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Merge `updateUnitLogicTimed` + `applyLiquidSteering` into single `updateUnitFull(unit, time)` call in bucket loop. Eliminates double function call overhead. |
| 1b | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Pre-compute `unit.flowTarget` and `unit.flowField` in a single pass before bucket loop (already done — just verify). |

**Test:** Unit count unchanged. Profile bucket loop: should show ~15% fewer calls.

### Phase 2: Separation Optimization (2-3 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 2a | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Replace full-sweep `applySeparation()` with per-cell iteration. Only iterate occupied SpatialHash cells (not all units). ~30-50% fewer queries at 5000 units. |
| 2b | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Cache separation results per-cell per-frame. Reuse in `applyLiquidSteering()` (velocity alignment already piggybacks). |
| 2c | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Add `SEPARATION_RADIUS_SQ = 324` constant (precomputed). Replace `distSq < 324` check with constant comparison. |

**Test:** 5000-unit stress test. Separation frame time: < 2ms (was ~5ms).

### Phase 3: Target Scan Optimization (2 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 3a | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Move `_buildEngagementMap()` to `update()` top-level (once per frame, not per scan). Store as `_engagementMap`. |
| 3b | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | In `scanForTargets()`, read `_engagementMap` instead of rebuilding. |
| 3c | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Add distance-LOD: units > 500px from nearest enemy use `scanInterval = 1000ms` (was 500ms for all). |

**Test:** Profile scan phase. Target: < 1ms/frame at 3000 combat units.

### Phase 4: Adaptive Path Memory (1 day)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 4a | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Replace hardcoded `200` with `maxPathLength = Math.min(300, Math.max(80, mapWidth / 10))`. Scale with map size. |
| 4b | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Add `unit.pathMemoryUsed` tracker. Log when cap hit (debug mode only). |

**Test:** 4096x4096 map. Verify no path truncation at default zoom.

---

## 3. LiquidCombat Scaling

**Current state:** Pressure grid (SpatialHash cells), contact lines (formation pairs), velocity alignment. All precomputed in `precompute()` before UnitSystem bucket pass. Per-unit forces applied in `applyLiquidSteering()`.

**Problems identified:**
- `precompute()` iterates all units twice (pressure + contact). At 5000 units, ~1ms per pass.
- Contact line detection uses AABB gap between formations — breaks when formations overlap (gap = 0, strength = 1 for all pairs).
- `getContactForce()` linearly scans all contact lines per unit — O(units × contactLines). At 200 contact lines + 3000 units = 600K iterations.
- Velocity alignment queries SpatialHash per unit — duplicate of separation query.
- `isCivilian()` check runs per unit per phase — branch prediction friendly but redundant when called 3x per unit.

### Phase 1: Precompute Fusion (1-2 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 1a | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.ts` | Merge pressure grid + contact line detection into single unit iteration. Build both structures in one pass over `allUnits`. Eliminates O(n) second pass. |
| 1b | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.ts` | Pre-filter civilian check once at top: `const military = allUnits.filter(u => !isCivilian(u))`. Use `military` for both passes. |
| 1c | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.ts` | Cache `military` array per-frame. Reuse in `getAlignmentVelocity()`. |

**Test:** 5000-unit stress test. `precompute()` time: < 0.5ms (was ~1ms).

### Phase 2: Contact Line Optimization (2-3 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 2a | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.ts` | Add contact line spatial index: `Map<string, ContactLine[]>` keyed by grid cell. `getContactForce()` queries only nearby cells instead of scanning all lines. |
| 2b | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.ts` | Fix AABB overlap bug: when `gap < 0`, set `strength = 1.0` (fully engaged) instead of `1 - 0/COUNTACT_RANGE`. |
| 2c | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.ts` | Cap `contactLines` array at 500. Sort by strength descending. Drop weakest beyond cap. |

**Test:** 2000-unit battle (1000v1000). Contact line count: < 200. `getContactForce()` time: < 0.1ms.

### Phase 3: Velocity Alignment Deduplication (1-2 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 3a | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.ts` | Remove `getAlignmentVelocity()` SpatialHash query. Use separation's cached neighbor list. |
| 3b | `game/systems/UnitSystem.ts` | Pass separation neighbors to `liquidCombat.applyAlignment(unit, neighbors)`. Avoid second query. |
| 3c | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.ts` | `applyAlignment(unit, neighbors)`: compute avg velocity from pre-fetched neighbors. |

**Test:** Profile `applyLiquidSteering()` per unit. Target: < 0.05ms (was ~0.1ms).

### Phase 4: Force Tuning & Debug Visualization (2 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 4a | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.ts` | Add `debugForceGraphics` (optional). Draw pressure arrows, contact normals. Gate behind `scene.debugMode`. |
| 4b | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.ts` | Tune constants: `PRESSURE_FORCE_MAX`, `CONTACT_BACKWARD_FORCE`, `ALIGN_STRENGTH` based on stress test. |
| 4c | `game/systems/LiquidCombatSystem.test.ts` (new) | Unit tests for pressure gradient calculation, contact line detection, alignment averaging. |

**Test:** Visual: armies collide → front compresses → lateral flow visible. Perf: 5000-unit battle < 2ms total liquid combat.

---

## 4. Atmospheric Performance

**Current state:** 20 cloud sprites, bloom (PostFX), vignette, seasonal tint (Graphics.fillRect), wind sway (sine). PostFX toggle. Seasonal tint dirty flag.

**Problems identified:**
- Bloom is a full-screen GPU pass — dominates frame time on iGPUs (Intel UHD, M1 integrated)
- 20 cloud sprites each updated every frame — O(20) per frame even when zoomed out (clouds invisible)
- Seasonal tint `fillRect` covers entire viewport even when alpha ~ 0 — wasted GPU fill
- `getWindSway()` called per-tree per-frame — no caching, redundant sine computation
- No LOD: atmospheric effects run at same cost regardless of zoom level

### Phase 1: Cloud Culling (1 day)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 1a | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Add viewport culling to cloud update. Skip update for clouds outside camera bounds + 500px padding. |
| 1b | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Pool cloud sprites: max 12 active, recycle off-screen clouds. Reduce from 20 to 12. |
| 1c | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Skip cloud update entirely when `cam.zoom < 0.5` (zoomed out — clouds invisible). |

**Test:** Profile cloud update. Target: < 0.1ms (was ~0.3ms).

### Phase 2: Bloom Adaptive Quality (2 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 2a | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Add zoom-based bloom resolution: `bloomQuality = clamp(cam.zoom, 0.25, 1.0)`. Lower zoom = lower resolution bloom pass. |
| 2b | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Add FPS-gated bloom: if FPS < 30 for 2 consecutive seconds, reduce `bloomEffect.strength` by 20%. Restore when FPS > 45. |
| 2c | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Add `setBloomQuality(quality: 'high' | 'medium' | 'low')` method. Low = no bloom, Medium = half-res, High = full. |

**Test:** Intel UHD 620 benchmark. Bloom cost: < 2ms (was ~5ms).

### Phase 3: Wind Sway Cache (1 day)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 3a | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Cache wind sway per-position: `Map<string, { value: number; time: number }>`. Reuse for 100ms. |
| 3b | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Quantize positions to 32px grid before cache lookup. Reduce cache size. |
| 3c | `game/systems/CullingSystem.ts` | Call `atmosphericSystem.getWindSway()` in tree visual update (already has per-tree iteration). |

**Test:** 1000 visible trees. Wind sway cost: < 0.05ms (was ~0.2ms).

### Phase 4: Seasonal Tint Optimization (1 day)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 4a | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Skip `fillRect` when `alpha < 0.005`. Already partially implemented — verify no edge cases. |
| 4b | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Use `Phaser.GameObjects.Rectangle` instead of `Graphics` for seasonal tint. Avoids Graphics clear/fill overhead. |
| 4c | `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts` | Cache tint color/alpha. Only create new Rectangle when target changes (not every frame). |

**Test:** Profile seasonal tint. Target: < 0.05ms (was ~0.3ms on large viewport).

---

## 5. React-Phaser Bridge Improvements

**Current state:** Dual-channel bridge. React→Phaser via `window.dispatchEvent(CustomEvent)` → `App.tsx` bridge → `gameInstance.events.emit()`. Phaser→React via `scene.events.emit(EVENTS.UPDATE_STATS, ...)` → `App.tsx` listener → `setStats()`. 20+ event types in `EVENTS` constant.

**Problems identified:**
- `setStats()` called every frame (60fps) triggers full React re-render tree — `GameUI` + children
- `window.dispatchEvent(CustomEvent)` for React→Phaser is indirect — adds DOM event overhead
- No event batching: rapid selection changes fire multiple `SELECTION_CHANGED` events
- `PhaserGame.tsx` recreates game instance on every prop change (faction, mapMode, etc.) — full destroy/recreate
- No cleanup verification: event listeners added in `useEffect` may leak if `gameInstance` changes

### Phase 1: Stats Throttling (1-2 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 1a | `game/MainScene.ts` | Throttle `UPDATE_STATS` emission: emit max 10fps (100ms interval), not 60fps. |
| 1b | `App.tsx` | Add `useMemo` for `GameUI` props derived from `stats`. Prevent unnecessary re-renders. |
| 1c | `components/GameUI.tsx` | Add `React.memo()` to `GameUI` component. Compare `stats` shallow-equal. |

**Test:** Profile React render. Target: 10 re-renders/sec (was 60). No visual lag on resource counters.

### Phase 2: Direct Bridge (2-3 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 2a | `App.tsx` | Replace `window.dispatchEvent(CustomEvent)` with `gameInstance.events.emit()` directly. Store `gameInstance` in ref (already available). |
| 2b | `App.tsx` | Remove all `window.addEventListener('...')` handlers in `useEffect`. Replace with direct `gameInstance.events.emit()`. |
| 2c | `constants.ts` | Add missing event names to `EVENTS` object (currently using magic strings like `'request-set-formation'`, `'clear-selection'`, `'save-game'`). |

**Test:** Verify all React→Phaser commands work (build, spawn, formation, stance, research, save/load).

### Phase 3: Event Batching (2-3 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 3a | `game/MainScene.ts` | Add `emitBatched(event, data, intervalMs)`: queue event, emit at most once per `intervalMs`. |
| 3b | `game/MainScene.ts` | Apply batching to `SELECTION_CHANGED`, `UPDATE_STATS`, `BUILDING_SELECTED`. |
| 3c | `components/GameUI.tsx` | Use `useDeferredValue` for `selectedCount` to defer non-critical UI updates. |

**Test:** Rapid selection changes (click 10 units in 100ms). Verify single `SELECTION_CHANGED` emission.

### Phase 4: Game Lifecycle Safety (1-2 days)

| Step | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| 4a | `components/PhaserGame.tsx` | Add `useRef` guard: skip destroy/recreate if only `stressTestConfig` changes. Use `game.scene.restart()` instead. |
| 4b | `App.tsx` | Add cleanup verification: in `useEffect` return, check `gameInstance.events.off()` for all listeners. Log warning if any missing. |
| 4c | `App.tsx` | Add `useEffect` dependency audit: ensure `gameInstance` is the only dependency for bridge listener setup. |

**Test:** Start game → quit → restart. No console errors, no leaked listeners.

---

## Dependency Graph

```
Phase 1 (all systems)  →  Phase 2  →  Phase 3  →  Phase 4
     ↑                      ↑           ↑           ↑
  Pathfinder             UnitSystem  LiquidCombat  Atmospheric
  (foundation)           (consumes)  (piggybacks)  (independent)
```

**Recommended order:** Pathfinder P1 → UnitSystem P1 → LiquidCombat P1 → Atmospheric P1 → (all P2 in parallel) → (all P3 in parallel) → (all P4 in parallel).

---

## Risks & Assumptions

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| JPS iterative conversion may change path output | Unit test: compare old recursive vs new iterative on 100 grids. Paths must be identical. |
| Priority queue introduces latency for idle units | Cap idle priority queue depth at 1000. Drop oldest idle paths beyond cap. |
| Contact line spatial index may double memory | Cap at 500 lines. Monitor `performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize`. |
| Bloom adaptive quality may cause visual pops | Lerp bloom strength over 2 seconds, not instant. |
| React throttle may cause stale stats display | Show "..." indicator when stats are stale > 500ms. |
| Direct bridge bypasses DOM event bus | No dependency — Phaser events are in-process. DOM events were always redundant. |

---

## Unresolved Questions

1. **Pathfinder:** Should JPS support weighted grids (biome costs) or stick to uniform? Current implementation treats costs as post-hoc — may produce suboptimal paths in heterogeneous terrain.
2. **LiquidCombat:** Should contact lines support more than 2 owners (free-for-all)? Current code assumes binary owner=0 vs owner=1.
3. **Atmospheric:** Should bloom be user-configurable per quality preset (Low/Medium/High/Custom)? Currently only a single slider.
4. **React-Phaser:** Should stats emission be pushed from MainScene or pulled by React (polling)? Push is simpler but creates coupling.

## Handoff

**File:** `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts`

**Changes:**
- Added `activeClouds`, `cloudPool` arrays + `maxActiveClouds = 12`.
- `createClouds()` — now spawns 20 sprites into pool (hidden, `active=false`), no initial scatter. Removed dead `getSpawnBounds()`.
- `recycleCloud(cloud)` — hides, drops from `activeClouds`, pushes back to `cloudPool` (no viewBounds param).
- `spawnCloudAtEdge(viewBounds)` — pops from pool, positions at random view edge, marks active. Fixed `x: number, y: number` definite-assignment (init `= 0`).
- `maintainActiveClouds(viewBounds)` — refills active list up to `maxActiveClouds` while pool non-empty.
- `update()` cloud block — split on `cloudActive = postFXEnabled && cam.zoom >= 0.5`:
  - `!cloudActive` → recycle all active (skips update, zero overhead) — covers both PostFX-off and **zoom < 0.5**.
  - else → 500px-padded `viewBounds`, `maintainActiveClouds`, then per-frame loop updates only clouds inside bounds; **viewport culling** recycles any cloud outside bounds+500px.

**Behavior implemented:**
1. Viewport culling — skip/recycle clouds outside camera bounds + 500px padding.
2. Pooling — max 12 active, recycle off-screen into pool, refill from edges.
3. Skip entirely when `cam.zoom < 0.5` (also PostFX off).

All 107 tests pass. tsc clean, ESLint clean. The SFX loader noise is pre-existing (test fixture asset fetch), unrelated.

## Handoff

**File:** `game/systems/AtmosphericSystem.ts`

**Changes:**
- Added `activeClouds`, `cloudPool` arrays + `maxActiveClouds = 12`.
- `createClouds()` — now spawns 20 sprites into pool (hidden, `active=false`), no initial scatter. Removed dead `getSpawnBounds()`.
- `recycleCloud(cloud)` — hides, drops from `activeClouds`, pushes back to `cloudPool` (no viewBounds param).
- `spawnCloudAtEdge(viewBounds)` — pops from pool, positions at random view edge, marks active. Fixed `x: number, y: number` definite-assignment (init `= 0`).
- `maintainActiveClouds(viewBounds)` — refills active list up to `maxActiveClouds` while pool non-empty.
- `update()` cloud block — split on `cloudActive = postFXEnabled && cam.zoom >= 0.5`:
  - `!cloudActive` → recycle all active (skips update, zero overhead) — covers both PostFX-off and **zoom < 0.5**.
  - else → 500px-padded `viewBounds`, `maintainActiveClouds`, then per-frame loop updates only clouds inside bounds; **viewport culling** recycles any cloud outside bounds+500px.

**Behavior implemented:**
1. Viewport culling — skip/recycle clouds outside camera bounds + 500px padding.
2. Pooling — max 12 active, recycle off-screen into pool, refill from edges.
3. Skip entirely when `cam.zoom < 0.5` (also PostFX off).

**Verification:** `tsc --noEmit` clean; `eslint --max-warnings 0` clean; `vitest run` 107/107 pass.

**Risk:** Spawn-biased across 4 edges; right-edge spawns drift out next frame (minor churn, harmless). No new tests added (task scoped; existing suite green).
